title: A Wretched Hive
summary: The heroes travel to Takodana to infiltrate Varga Besadii Drokko's fortress, posing as entertainment to discover where Varth's skimmed fortune is hidden. Over several days in the Hutt's court, they navigate gladiatorial spectacle, slave traders, an ISB double agent, and a nighttime assassination attempt — slowly uncovering that the account location is stored in a Cybot Galactica Model VII courier cybernetic surgically embedded in Varga's skull. The crew never extracts the data; an assassination attempt triggers a cascade — Denia is discovered in the dungeons, Demos betrays Varga, and Varga flees to Bespin. The escape costs lives: Demos dies fighting, Varth executes Raden, and the crew escapes with Cloud City intel, Figg & Associates, and the implant specs from TC-663 — but not the account data itself.

scenes.title: Blackwind Point
scenes.subtitle: The Landing Tax
scenes.readAloud:
You disembark at Blackwind Point — a muddy, desperate shantytown on the far shore of Nymeve Lake. The air is thick with the smell of rotting vegetation and desperation. Refugees huddle in makeshift shelters while criminals eye your gear with open hunger.

The growl of repulsor-bikes cuts through the noise. A swoop gang circles your landing pad, engines revving. Their leader — a scarred human woman with a vibro-blade strapped to her leg — pulls up and kills her engine.

"Welcome to the other side of the lake. Landing tax is five hundred credits. Non-negotiable."
scenes.gmNotes:
This scene is a standalone social encounter with a combat fallback. Kessra and the Vipers demand 500 credits. The crew either pays, talks their way out, or fights.

KESSRA CONSEQUENCE GATE: This is the most important mechanical note in the scene. How the crew handles Kessra determines a conditional event inside Varga's fortress later. If they humiliate her (fight and win decisively, or intimidate her publicly), Kessra takes it personally. She reappears inside Varga's fortress during the court phase (Part 2, Scene 3) as a hired security contractor and springs an aviary ambush targeting specific heroes by name. If they pay or handle it diplomatically, Kessra does NOT reappear — no grudge, no aviary scene.

PAYING: If the crew pays the 500cr, Kessra takes it and waves them through. The Vipers watch but don't hassle them further. The crew is now marked as easy targets — pickpockets and grifters will approach them in the encampment. Word spreads that the newcomers fold under pressure.

FIGHTING: If it turns violent, Kessra fights from her swoop. The Vipers fan out and use hit-and-run tactics. The mud is difficult terrain for the crew but the swoops ignore it. If Kessra is beaten, the gang scatters. Local respect earned — but Kessra remembers.

AFTER THE ENCOUNTER: Regardless of outcome, the crew is now standing in Blackwind Point with a job to do — find Warrick Raden. Varth has briefed them: a Devaronian fixer who can get them into Varga's court. All they have is a name. The encampment stretches out before them — refugees, junk traders, cantinas, spice dealers. Time to start asking questions.

scenes.title: Working the Encampment
scenes.subtitle: Finding Raden
scenes.readAloud:
Blackwind Point is a sprawl of desperation and opportunism. Muddy lanes wind between scrap-metal shelters and sagging tarpaulin stalls. A Rodian hawking stolen power cells argues with a Gran over a crate of expired ration packs. Somewhere a child is crying. A pair of Aqualish dockhands sit on overturned fuel drums, watching you with flat, hostile eyes.

Somewhere in this place — or beyond it — a Devaronian fixer named Warrick Raden is hiding. Varth said he could get you inside Varga's court. All you have is a name and a description. Start asking questions.

The encampment is best run as five ordered beats — a slow social descent from the muddy thoroughfare, into The Drowned Sarlacc cantina, out through the market stalls, past the refugee tents, and finally into the swamp-edge water-haulers' dock where the trail closes on the filtration plant.
scenes.gmNotes:
GROUP CHALLENGE: This scene uses a Victory Point (VP) accumulation mechanic. The crew fans out across Blackwind Point and works different angles to track down Raden's location. Each PC picks a discipline and describes their approach.

MECHANICS:
- Tier 1 / Power 3 across all disciplines
- Each PC rolls Control (stepped down 1 die for T1). Control 4+ = success.
- On success, roll Power vs P3 to determine effect tier:
  • Fleeting (Power loses or ties) = 1 VP
  • Masterful (Power wins) = 2 VP
  • Legendary (Power wins decisively) = 3 VP
  • Mastery (Control 8+) = +1 VP added to the tier result
- 10 VP total = they've pinpointed Raden's location
- Below 10, they can attempt more rolls or go looking with incomplete info

FAILURE CONSEQUENCE: A failed Control roll (below 4) means someone noticed the crew asking around. Word travels through the encampment. Each failure increases the risk that Varga's people — or the Trandoshan hit squad already hunting Raden — learn that someone else is looking for the same man. The GM should narrate the growing tension: a merchant who suddenly clams up, a figure watching from a doorway, whispered conversations that stop when the crew approaches.

VP THRESHOLDS — Read aloud or paraphrase at each threshold:

3 VP: 'A Devaronian? Yeah, I saw one drinking at the Drowned Sarlacc three, four days ago. Kept to himself. Haven't seen him since.' — A sighting, but cold. He was here.

5 VP: 'That Devaronian — he was talking to old Mekka the parts dealer. Bought a bunch of ration packs and a portable charge cell. Like someone planning to disappear.' — He's hiding somewhere, stocking up to stay gone.

7 VP: 'Two days ago I saw a Devaronian running through the east market. Some of Varga's boys were on his tail. He cut toward the swamp and they pulled up at the tree line. Didn't follow him in.' — Direction established. He went into the swamp.

9 VP: 'There's an old water filtration plant out past the swamp edge. Imperial-era, been abandoned for years. Saw smoke from that direction yesterday morning. Nobody goes out there.' — Specific location narrowed down.

10 VP: 'That's where your Devaronian is. The filtration plant. I hauled water purifiers out there two years back — there's a maintenance shed on the west side with a working lock. If he's hiding anywhere, it's that shed.' — Confirmed. Go.

ENCOURAGING DIFFERENT APPROACHES: Each PC should describe their approach narratively. The discipline they choose should match what they're doing. The GM provides the VP threshold readout based on total accumulated VP, not individual rolls. Let the players feel the trail building — each piece of information makes the next question more specific.

SCENE ENDS: When the crew hits 10 VP or when they decide they've heard enough and want to go looking with what they have. If they leave before 10 VP, they'll need to search the swamp edge — add a complication to Scene 3 (Raden is harder to find, they stumble into his trip-wires, etc.).

ENCOUNTER NPCs: The encampment should feel alive. Use these locals as color and information sources. Not every NPC has intel — some are just texture. The crew should feel like they're working a real place, not just rolling dice.

npcs.name: Mekka
npcs.notes: Runs a stall near the east market. Sold Raden ration packs and a portable charge cell three days ago. Knows Raden was stocking up to hide.
npcs.behaviour: Shrewd and unhelpful unless given a reason to talk. Credits loosen his tongue. Responds well to Charm. Clams up under Intimidate — he's been shaken down too many times.
dialogue: "A Devaronian? I see a lot of Devaronians. What's in it for me?"
"He bought survival supplies. Ration packs, charge cell, water tabs. Paid in cash — Imperial credits, not Hutt scrip. That's unusual around here."
"I don't know where he went. I sell parts, not directions."

npcs.name: Drelk
npcs.notes: Works the landing pads. Saw Raden fleeing Varga's enforcers two days ago. Watched him cut toward the swamp. Doesn't want trouble.
npcs.behaviour: Sullen and cautious. Will talk if approached without hostility. Responds to shared drinks or a show of solidarity. Won't talk to anyone who looks Imperial.
dialogue: "I mind my own business. You should try it."
"Two days ago. East market. Your Devaronian was running hard. Varga's boys were on him. He went for the swamp — they stopped at the tree line. Smart of them. Stupid of him."
"The swamp takes people. If he went in there, he's either dead or more desperate than I thought."

npcs.name: Nola Shar
npcs.notes: A mother with two children. Arrived from Felucia three weeks ago. She saw smoke from the filtration plant yesterday morning.
npcs.behaviour: Exhausted and wary. Won't volunteer information unless she feels safe. Responds to kindness — a ration pack, a kind word, asking about her children. She doesn't know who Raden is specifically, but she knows the filtration plant.
dialogue: "Please — we don't want trouble. We just need to get to the next transport."
"The filtration plant? It's been abandoned since the Republic fell. But I saw smoke from that direction yesterday when I was washing clothes at the creek. Someone's out there."
"Be careful near the swamp. There are things in that water."

npcs.name: Gorr the Barkeep
npcs.notes: Runs The Drowned Sarlacc — the only cantina in Blackwind Point. Raden drank here four days ago. Gorr doesn't care about Raden but he cares about his bar.
npcs.behaviour: Four arms, three of which are always busy. Hospitable to paying customers. Has no loyalty to anyone but himself. Will trade information for credits or a favor.
dialogue: "Devaronian? Red skin, horns, looked like he hadn't slept in a week? Sat in the back corner four days ago. Nursed one drink for three hours. Then left."
"He was asking about the swamp — what's out there, who goes there. I told him the same thing I tell everyone: nothing good."
"You want another round or are you going to keep asking questions I'm not getting paid for?"

npcs.name: Greez Thakka
npcs.notes: Hauls water purification equipment to settlements around the lake. Knows the filtration plant intimately — he serviced it two years ago. Can describe the maintenance shed.
npcs.behaviour: Gentle and cooperative. Speaks through a translator unit. Happy to help if asked politely. Doesn't understand why anyone would hide at the filtration plant.
dialogue: "The filtration plant? Yes, I know it well. I serviced the purification units there two years ago, before the last of the operators left."
"There is a maintenance shed on the west side. It has a working lock — Imperial standard, five-digit code. Whoever went in would need to slice it or have the code."
"It is not a comfortable place. But it is hidden. The swamp growth has nearly swallowed it."

scenes.hazards: The encampment itself is not physically dangerous, but drawing too much attention is. Failed investigation attempts alert Varga's network or the Trandoshan hit squad already hunting Raden.

decisions.consequence: Complete picture — exact location of Raden's hiding spot. Clean approach to the filtration plant.
Must search the swamp edge. Raden's trip-wires catch the crew off guard. Complications at the filtration plant.

narrativeLinks.note: VP total determines how prepared the crew is when they arrive at the filtration plant.

encounters.name: Beat 1 — Onto the Thoroughfare
encounters.trigger: Crew leaves the landing pad after Kessra is resolved
encounters.description: The mud thoroughfare opens out. Refugees, junk traders, spice runners, and a Rodian fence shouting prices over the noise. Whoever the crew talks to here will only give them surface read on the encampment — who runs which stall, where the cantina is, which lane to avoid after dark. Nobody on the thoroughfare knows Raden by name. They know the categories he fits — Devaronian, ran with Varga, hiding. That's the entry point.
encounters.tactics: VP-soft beat. The crew is orienting. Award 0-1 VP per check on the group challenge — this is the warm-up. Accept narrative hooks more than dice. The Kessra outcome from p1-s1 colors this beat: if the crew was marked as easy targets (paid the tax), pickpockets and grifters approach now and the GM can run a quick optional theft attempt for color. If the crew was respected (intimidated or charmed Kessra), local heads nod as they pass and one stallkeeper waves them toward The Drowned Sarlacc unprompted. Ends when the crew picks a direction — almost always toward the cantina.

encounters.name: Beat 2 — The Drowned Sarlacc
encounters.trigger: Crew enters the cantina (the only one in Blackwind Point)
encounters.description: Smoky, low-ceilinged, four-arms behind the bar. Gorr the Besalisk barkeep runs the only social hub in Blackwind Point — a battered cantina that serves as Raden's last confirmed sighting four days ago. This is the highest-yield beat in the encampment. The cantina is also where a Trandoshan spotter is sitting in the corner watching everyone who asks about Devaronians. The crew can pump Gorr for the cold sighting (3 VP threshold), buy drinks for table-side regulars who saw Raden's purchases (Mekka lead, 5 VP threshold), or ask after the figure who chased a Devaronian east two days ago (7 VP threshold). Gorr will trade information for credits, a favor, or a particularly entertaining reason.
encounters.tactics: PRIMARY VP BEAT. This is where most of the group challenge plays out — Charm and Skulduggery shine here, Investigation works the regulars at the side tables. Most VP across the scene should be earned in this beat. THREAT BUILD: The Trandoshan spotter is non-combat in this scene but becomes a real entity. If a PC succeeds an Insight check (Resist 3) they spot the spotter, which gives the crew a head start on the s4 fight (one Trandoshan loses surprise). If the crew fails too many Control rolls (3+) in this beat, the spotter recognizes the pattern and slips out the back to alert the hit squad — accelerates the s4 timeline by an in-fiction hour.

encounters.name: Beat 3 — Mekka's Stall and the East Market
encounters.trigger: Crew follows the Sarlacc lead toward the east market
encounters.description: Mekka the Toydarian parts dealer remembers selling Raden ration packs, water tabs, and a portable charge cell three days ago. He'll trade what he knows for credits or a barter item from the gear list. Drelk the Aqualish dockhand drinks at the corner of the market when he's off shift — he watched Raden run through here with Varga's enforcers behind him, two days ago, and he watched the enforcers stop at the swamp tree line. Drelk responds badly to anyone who looks Imperial; he responds well to a shared bottle and a question that doesn't sound like a threat.
encounters.tactics: MID-VP BEAT — confirms direction. Mekka and Drelk are the 5-VP and 7-VP intel sources respectively. Charm and Investigation work best here. Mekka clams up under Intimidate (he's been shaken down too many times); Drelk shuts down under any approach that smells official. If a PC offers a ration pack or a piece of trade gear instead of credits, Mekka volunteers the charge-cell purchase as a bonus — pure flavor, but it confirms the crew is dealing with someone who's planning to stay hidden for weeks, not days.

encounters.name: Beat 4 — The Refugee Tents
encounters.trigger: Crew works the south side of the encampment
encounters.description: The refugee tarps stretch toward the swamp — Felucia evacuees, displaced Yavin contractors, a handful of Christophsis families who have been moving for years. Nola Shar and her two children are washing clothes in the creek. She saw smoke from the filtration plant yesterday morning. She doesn't know who's out there and she doesn't want to. She is exhausted, wary, and one short conversation away from breaking down. Kindness — a kind word, a ration pack for the kids, asking about her destination instead of about Raden — earns the intel. Anything else closes the door.
encounters.tactics: QUIET-VP BEAT — confirms location. Nola is the 9-VP threshold source. ONLY Charm and Insight are appropriate here; Intimidate against a refugee mother is a Comfort-style fail and the GM should narrate the entire camp turning cold for the rest of the scene (-2 VP from any further checks in this scene). If played with kindness, Nola also volunteers a warning about 'things in the swamp water' — flavor, but a crew that listens may bring extra rations or treat the swamp approach with appropriate caution in the next scene.

encounters.name: Beat 5 — Greez at the Water-Haulers' Dock
encounters.trigger: Crew finishes the trail at the lakeside dock — typically once they've banked 9+ VP
encounters.description: Greez Thakka, an Ithorian water hauler who works through a translator unit, is loading purification cartridges onto his skiff. He serviced the filtration plant two years ago and remembers it intimately — the maintenance shed on the west side, the working lock (Imperial-standard five-digit code), the swamp growth that has nearly swallowed the place. He'll happily describe everything he knows because he is constitutionally cheerful and slightly bored. He doesn't understand why anyone would hide there but he respects that people sometimes need to. The crew leaves with a complete picture: location, lock type, approach route, and the warning that a stranger has been camped there based on the smoke pattern.
encounters.tactics: CLOSING VP BEAT. Greez's intel completes the trail at the 10-VP threshold. He's the easiest social check in the encampment — Insight resist 1 — because he's actively trying to be helpful. If the crew hits this beat with fewer than 9 VP, he can still close the trail himself if asked the right question (Investigation check at Resist 2, no Control floor — almost automatic). If the crew skipped this beat entirely and went straight to the swamp, they'll discover Raden's trip-wires the hard way (per the existing s3 fallback). Greez also volunteers, unprompted, that he heard 'someone heavy' walking around the southern edge of the swamp two nights ago — first seed of the Trandoshan presence, before the spotter recognition pays off in s4.

scenes.title: The Filtration Plant
scenes.subtitle: Finding Raden
scenes.readAloud:
The swamp thickens as you push past the encampment's edge. Gnarled trees hang with curtains of moss. The ground turns soft, then wet. Insects swarm in clouds around every step.

After twenty minutes of trudging through knee-deep muck, the trees open onto a clearing dominated by a rusted industrial structure — the old water filtration plant. Pipes jut from the walls at odd angles, crusted with mineral deposits. Most of the windows are dark. But through a crack in one of the maintenance shed shutters on the west side, you catch the faint glow of a charge lamp.

Something moves behind the shutter. A shadow. Then silence.

Then a voice — sharp, shaking, and speaking Basic with a Devaronian accent:

"Don't come any closer. I will shoot."
scenes.gmNotes:
[map:filtration-plant]

ARRIVAL: If the crew reached 10 VP in the group challenge, they know exactly where Raden is hiding — the maintenance shed on the west side. They can approach directly and with confidence. If they left the encampment with fewer than 10 VP, they need to search the plant grounds. Add complications: they trip Raden's crude perimeter alarms (toppled cans on wire), hear him before they see him, or have to search multiple buildings before finding the right one.

RADEN'S STATE: Warrick Raden is a Devaronian in his forties. He's been hiding here for three days. He's sleep-deprived, malnourished, and terrified. He has a blaster aimed at the door — his hands are shaking. He set crude trip-wires around the maintenance shed and has been surviving on the ration packs he bought from Mekka.

Raden thought Varth was dead — captured by the Empire and executed. When the crew mentions Varth's name, Raden's reaction is visceral: shock, then relief, then fear again. Varth being alive means there's a plan. A plan means danger.

RADEN'S BACKSTORY: Raden was a middleman in Varga's financial network. After Varth was captured, Raden skimmed credits — thought no one was watching. Varga found out. Raden has been running ever since. He has hand-drawn maps of Varga's fortress from when he worked the operation, guard shift patterns he memorized, and intimate knowledge of Varga's paranoid habits.

RADEN WILL NOT GO BACK: This is the critical narrative beat. Raden absolutely refuses to return to Varga's fortress. Varga sent Trandoshans to kill him. He watched them from the tree line. He knows what awaits him if he goes back — the gladiator pit, a public execution, or worse. No amount of persuasion will make him willingly walk back into that fortress. He'll say: 'I'm dead if I step foot on that dock. You know it. I know it.'

However, Raden WILL share intel. If the crew earns his trust (Charm, showing Varth's message, genuine empathy), he opens up fully — hand-drawn maps, guard rotations, Varga's daily patterns, TC-663's location, guest quarters layout, and suggestions for a cover identity. He knows Varga is hosting a delegation of high rollers and entertainment — gladiators, gamblers, mercenaries. He can coach the crew on how to present themselves convincingly. He just won't be there with them.

THE VARTH OPTION (DARK PATH): If the crew contacts Varth via encrypted comlink (either because Raden is being difficult or because they want a stronger entry), Varth provides a cold, pragmatic suggestion: 'Varga wants Raden. Deliver him. A fugitive returned in chains is worth more than any cover story. That's your entry ticket — and Varga owes you a favor before you've even walked through the door.'

Varth says this without emotion. He's ex-Imperial. He thinks in assets and leverage. If the heroes push back, he doesn't argue — he simply says, 'It's your call. I'm telling you what works.' This is the first real glimpse of Varth's pragmatic ruthlessness and foreshadows his willingness to sacrifice people for the mission.

DELIVERING RADEN: If the heroes decide to take Raden by force, he fights — desperately, poorly, but he fights. He has a blaster and he knows the terrain around the filtration plant. This should feel ugly. He's not a soldier. He's a terrified man who just helped them and they're dragging him to his death. If a hero has any moral compass, this should cost something.

Alternatively, the heroes might trick Raden — Deception to convince him they're taking him somewhere safe, then deliver him to Varga. This is cleaner mechanically but even darker morally.

RADEN STAYS BEHIND (LIGHT PATH): If the heroes treat Raden well and don't deliver him, he stays at the filtration plant or makes his way off-world. He gives them everything he knows and wishes them luck. 'Find TC-663. Use Switch's code phrase if you have it. Six-Six will help you from the inside.' The heroes enter the fortress on their own cover identity, without a gift for Varga.

NARRATIVE CONSEQUENCES: Delivering Raden creates a dramatically different entry to the fortress (Scene 5) and directly sets up the 'Execution of Raden' court event in Part 2. Protecting Raden means the heroes must earn Varga's trust purely on merit — harder, but morally clean.

THE NEGOTIATION: How the crew handles Raden determines his cooperation level:

- CALM / NEGOTIATE: Raden cooperates willingly with intel. He provides detailed fortress maps, guard rotations, Varga's daily patterns, the location of TC-663, and where guests are quartered. He stays behind but is genuinely grateful.

- THREATEN (without delivering): Raden gives minimum intel. Maps only, no details on routines or TC-663. He tells them to get out and never come back.

- DELIVER TO VARGA (Varth's option): Raden is taken by force or deception. The crew arrives at the fortress with a valuable gift. Triggers the Execution event in Part 2. Dark Side moment.

RADEN'S OFFER: Once calmed, Raden proposes the plan: he can get the crew inside Varga's court as 'entertainment' — gladiators, gamblers, or mercenaries. Varga is hosting a delegation of high rollers and business partners. He wants spectacle. Raden can vouch for the crew's credentials.

SCENE ENDS: When Raden's cooperation is established and the plan is agreed upon. Then the Trandoshans arrive — transition to Scene 4.

encounters.name: Beat 1 — First Contact at the Door
encounters.trigger: Crew approaches the maintenance shed
encounters.description: A voice through the shutter — Devaronian, sleep-deprived, panicking with a blaster aimed at the door. 'Don't come any closer. I will shoot.' The crew has to talk him down before they can talk to him. Mention Varth's name early: it is the single key that unlocks Raden's door without a fight. If the crew has 10 VP from Scene 2, they know to avoid the trip-wires; if not, snapping a wire here triggers a warning shot through the door (no damage, but blown stealth and Raden's terror jumps another notch).
encounters.tactics: RUN: the existing Charm/Insight discipline checks (sc-a2s3-charm, sc-a2s3-insight) belong in this beat. Failure here doesn't end the scene — it just means more checks before Raden lowers the blaster. A clean Charm or Insight read (or invoking Varth's name with proof) earns the door opening. This beat ends when Raden lets the crew physically inside the shed and gestures to the workbench.

encounters.name: Beat 2 — Sitting Down with Raden (Conversation Overlay)
encounters.trigger: Raden lowers the blaster and lets the crew inside
encounters.description: The blaster goes onto the workbench within reach but no longer in his hand. Raden sits on a cargo crate with his back to the wall and tells the crew, plainly, that he is one wrong word from bolting into the swamp. He invites their questions. This is a structured social scene — the Raden conversation overlay. Launch the [raden-blackwind] conversation from the Conversation panel.
encounters.tactics: GM ACTION: Open the Conversation panel in the Command Bridge and launch [raden-blackwind]. Players ask questions through the player overlay; GM delivers Raden's responses one beat at a time. Raden starts at Comfort 2 — significantly lower than Maya (Comfort 4) or Varth (Comfort 5), reflecting how much closer he is to bolting than either of them ever was. The fastest comfort gain in the tree is leading with proof Varth is alive. The Trandoshan boots in the swamp are the GM's hard exit lever — call them out the moment the conversation feels done, or sooner if comfort drops to 1. Mirrors the Maya conversation's structure with a tighter, terror-driven texture. End the scene when accessible topics run out, when comfort drops to 1, or when the GM is ready to hard-cut to s4.

encounters.name: Beat 3 — Spreading the Maps
encounters.trigger: After the conversation overlay closes — assuming Raden didn't bolt
encounters.description: Raden pulls a sheaf of folded flimsi out of his coat — hand-drawn maps of Varga's fortress, smudged from being slept on. He spreads them on the workbench and walks the crew through what they're looking at: throne room, dungeon corridor, kitchen approach, aviary, dock guard rotation, the two alternate entries (sewer outflow on the lake side, kitchen delivery hatch on the south wall). Whatever business topics the conversation surfaced get re-anchored to a physical map the crew can reference for the rest of the adventure. [map:varga-fortress]
encounters.tactics:
NO DICE — this is a delivery beat. Hand the players a printed or in-system fortress map if you have one — open [map:varga-fortress] and broadcast it to the crew so they can pin it for the rest of the adventure. The richness of this delivery is gated on the conversation outcome:
  • Comfort 4-5 at end of Beat 2: full map + every business topic Raden surfaced gets the full annotation. TC-663 protocol, Demos warning, Iron Ring/Lady Sinde context, Varga implant breadcrumb, aviary warning — all included.
  • Comfort 3: full map, only the topics the players actually asked about.
  • Comfort 2: maps only, no annotation. Players know the layout but not the politics.
  • Comfort 1 (Raden bolted): the crew finds the maps abandoned on the workbench when they search the shed. Layout only. No TC-663, no Demos, no implant warning.

encounters.name: Beat 4 — The Cover-Story Workshop
encounters.trigger: Raden has shared the maps and is willing to coach (Comfort 3+ at end of Beat 2)
encounters.description:
Raden walks the crew through the cover identity for each PC, one at a time. He uses the same three-sentence frame Varga responds to: a hook, a brag, a price. The crew workshops their own pitches against Raden's read of how Varga will hear them.

For the Muscle: hook (what kind of fighter), brag (their best previous purse), price (what they'll take to stay). For the Face: hook (what they sell — gambling, brokering, smooth talk), brag (their best previous mark), price (what they want from Varga's court). For the Tech: hook (specialization — repulsors, slicing, droids), brag (a trick Varga can immediately use), price (workshop access). For any other archetype, Raden adapts the frame on the fly. He coaches the rough edges out of each pitch and tells the crew exactly what NOT to say. (For a Hutt audience: never deference. Never flattery. Always sharp, slightly self-deprecating, and willing to insult a Desilijic clan rival by name.)

This is also where Varth, on the encrypted comlink from the Banshee, listens in and signs off on each cover. He adds one detail per identity that Raden didn't think of — a piece of fabricated history that palace records will corroborate, because Varth has already seeded it through TC-663. Varth and Raden working together on this beat is the only time in the campaign these two men will collaborate on the same task. Note the texture.
encounters.tactics:
NARRATIVE CHALLENGE: each PC describes their cover identity in the three-sentence frame. The GM treats their own pitch as the audition prep. Mechanically, this beat does NOT roll dice — but the quality of each PC's pitch sets the resist on the audition checks in s5 (the Deception check titled 'Maintaining cover identity under Varga's scrutiny' — note: its ID prefix is sc-a2s2-, a pre-existing naming quirk in this file; the check lives in adv2-p1-s5) as follows:
  • Strong, in-voice pitch with a hook/brag/price that matches the PC's actual sheet: -1 resist on their s5 audition.
  • Adequate pitch: standard resist as written.
  • Vague or off-tone pitch: +1 resist on their s5 audition.
This is the conversion of player creativity into mechanical advantage. Encourage players to lean in. Varth's encrypted-comm overlay is roleplay-only — he interjects between pitches with one or two lines of corrective humor and signs off the cover with 'Good. He'll buy that.' Raden gets the last word for each pitch. If Raden bolted (Comfort 1) or refused to coach (Comfort 2), this beat is replaced by a quieter scene where Varth alone runs the workshop over comlink — workable, but the crew loses Raden's lived knowledge of Varga's specific tells. ALL pitches are then run at +1 resist in s5.

scenes.title: The Hit Squad
scenes.subtitle: Protect Raden
scenes.readAloud:
Raden freezes mid-sentence. His eyes go wide.

"They found me."

You hear it now — the rhythmic squelch of heavy boots in the swamp. Multiple sets. Coming from at least two directions. Through the grimy windows of the filtration plant, you catch movement in the tree line: massive, scaled figures moving with predatory patience.

Trandoshans.

From the southern gate, a crash — then the grinding shriek of metal on metal. That jury-rigged utility droid Raden mentioned just activated. You hear it lurch forward on its treads, the cutting torch sparking to life with a high whine. Something roars — not the droid, one of the Trandoshans — followed by blaster fire and the crunch of the droid's chassis being torn apart. The sentry lasted about ten seconds.

Raden grabs your arm. "They're here to kill me. If I die, you don't get inside that fortress. Protect me."
scenes.gmNotes:
COMBAT ENCOUNTER: This is a straight fight with a protection objective. The crew must keep Raden alive while dealing with the Trandoshan hit squad.

[map:filtration-plant]

TRANDOSHAN TACTICS: The hit squad breaches from multiple entry points — they've been hunting Raden and they know the building. They use scent-tracking, which means steam concealment doesn't fully work against them (reduces to partial concealment). They work in pairs, using the cramped machinery to set up crossfires.

RADEN'S SENTRY DROID: The jury-rigged utility droid at the southern gate activates when the Trandoshans approach — and is destroyed almost immediately. It's a GNK-series utility chassis with a cutting torch and scrap armor, not a real combat unit. It serves as Raden's alarm system. When the crew hears it engage and die, that's their warning the Trandoshans have arrived. The wreckage partially blocks the southern gate approach (difficult terrain for one round as the Trandoshans push through it), buying the crew a few seconds to prepare.

ENVIRONMENTAL HAZARDS: The filtration plant is full of exploitable machinery. Steam pipes can be burst deliberately (Tech check) for area denial. Catwalks can be collapsed to block approaches. Cramped corridors between machinery limit movement to single-file — good for chokepoints, bad for being flanked. The settling tanks are difficult terrain (chest-deep water, slick biofilm). The treatment pool walkways are single-file only. Upper catwalks risk collapse with more than two people.

RADEN: He's not a fighter. He cowers behind cover, fires his blaster wildly if directly threatened (more dangerous to friendlies than enemies), and panics if anyone goes down. If a PC spends an action to direct him (Tactics or Leadership), he'll follow orders and stay in cover properly.

SCENE FAILURE: If Raden dies, the crew loses their primary intel source. They'd need to find another way to learn about the fortress — significantly harder and likely requiring Adventure-level improvisation.

AFTER THE FIGHT — THREE PATHS:

PATH A (LIGHT — Raden cooperated in Scene 3): Raden is shaken but alive. The hit squad proves his point — Varga will never stop hunting him. Raden gives his final intel briefing if he hasn't already: cover identity details, TC-663, guard rotations. Then he takes his chances in the swamp. 'I'll find a freighter at Blackwind. Get off-world. You've got what you need. Go.' The heroes take a skiff across Nymeve Lake on their own.

PATH B (DARK — Heroes decided to deliver Raden): After the fight, the heroes have Raden in their custody. He's terrified, begging, but restrained. The skiff ride across the lake is grim and silent. Raden knows what's coming. If any hero has second thoughts, this is the last chance to change course.

PATH C (VARTH'S OPTION EMERGES HERE): If the heroes protected Raden but haven't yet decided on the delivery option, this is where Varth's suggestion can surface. After the fight, the crew contacts Varth for extraction/next steps. Varth, hearing that Raden won't go back, makes his cold suggestion: 'You just killed the hit squad Varga sent. When those Trandoshans don't report back, Varga will know someone interfered. You need leverage. You have it — sitting right there.' This is dramatically effective because the heroes just risked their lives to save Raden, and now Varth is asking them to trade him.

The scene ends with the transition: the skiff ride across Nymeve Lake. Varga's fortress materializes through curtains of mist — a moss-covered stone ruin retrofitted with gaudy tech, blaster turrets, and garish banners. The next phase begins.

pacing.openingBeat: Heavy boots in the swamp. The sentry droid crashes and dies at the gate — ten seconds of grinding metal, then silence. 'They found me.'
pacing.risingAction: Trandoshans breach from multiple points through the jungle and over the sentry wreckage. Raden is panicking behind cover in the maintenance shed.
pacing.climax: The Trandoshans close from two directions, using the cramped pipe corridors and settling tank catwalks. The crew must use the environment — steam pipes, collapsing catwalks, chokepoints — or be overwhelmed.
pacing.resolution: Silence. The hit squad is down. Raden is alive but broken. The crew decides his fate — freedom or chains. Then the skiff ride across Nymeve Lake. Varga's fortress looms through the mist.

scenes.title: The Court of Varga
scenes.subtitle: The Throne Room
scenes.readAloud:
The skiff glides across Nymeve Lake through hanging curtains of mist. The fortress materializes ahead — a moss-covered stone ruin retrofitted with gaudy tech, blaster turrets, and gaudy banners bearing Varga's sigil. You dock at a landing platform ringed by Gamorrean guards.

Damp, torch-lit corridors smell of mold and roasting meat. The guards escort you deeper until you emerge into Varga's Throne Room — a sensory assault of thick smoke, frantic jizz-wailer music, and a crowd of sycophants, thieves, and scavengers.

At the far end, resting on a massive reinforced hover-sled, sits Varga the Hutt. He is bloated, scarred, and flanked by a polished silver protocol droid. Varga barks in Huttese, his deep voice shaking the room. The droid translates:

"The Mighty Varga is bored with beggars. Prove you are worth his air."

As Varga shifts on his hover-sled, you catch something — a faint blue flicker near his right temple, gone before you can focus on it. Probably a reflection off the protocol droid's chassis. Probably.
scenes.gmNotes:
[map:varga-fortress]

FORTRESS LAYOUT REFERENCE: If the crew received Raden's hand-drawn fortress map in adv2-p1-s3 Beat 3 (Comfort 2+), broadcast it here so it stays pinned for the rest of Part 2 — court audience, Iron Ring, infiltration routes, aviary, dungeon descent. The dock arrival in the read-aloud lines up with the dock entry on the map; the throne room they're walking into is the central chamber.

THIS SCENE HAS TWO ENTRY PATHS based on the heroes' choice regarding Raden in Scenes 3-4.

ENTRY PATH A — COVER IDENTITY (Raden stayed behind): The heroes arrive at the fortress dock on their own, presenting themselves using the cover identity Raden helped them build. They claim to be mercenaries, gladiators, or entertainers looking for work in Varga's court. Gate guards bring them before Varga for evaluation.

Varga demands an immediate demonstration. Each hero must prove their value:
- The Muscle gets a fight against a Gamorrean in the pit.
- The Face gets a battle of wits with courtiers.
- The Tech is ordered to fix Varga's hover-sled with a blaster at their head.
- Other specialists demonstrate as appropriate.

If heroes succeed, Varga welcomes them as 'guests' (prisoners with privileges). Without Raden as a gift, the heroes must earn trust purely on merit — which is harder but morally clean. Varga remains suspicious and Demos watches them closely.

ENTRY PATH B — RADEN IN CHAINS (Dark path): The heroes arrive with Raden bound and gagged. When the guards see the Devaronian, recognition flashes across their faces. The crew is fast-tracked past normal screening and brought directly before Varga.

Varga's reaction is dramatic — genuine delight. He laughs, a deep rumbling that shakes the room. 'You bring me a gift! The thief who stole from Besadii, delivered to my feet!' The Hutt immediately accepts the heroes into his court. No audition needed — delivering a fugitive proves they understand how business works.

This triggers the EXECUTION OF RADEN event (Part 2, Event 1). Varga keeps Raden in the gladiator pit cells until he decides on a suitably public punishment. The heroes are given guest quarters and treated well — but they now carry the weight of what they've done. Raden's eyes follow them as the Gamorreans drag him away.

CYBERNETIC BREADCRUMB #1: When Varga shifts on his hover-sled, observant heroes may notice a faint blue holographic flicker near his right temple — gone in an instant. This is the Cybot Galactica Model VII courier cybernetic's passive standby indicator, barely visible through Hutt skin. It looks like a light reflection. It is not. At this stage, there is nothing to act on — it's a planted detail for players to recall later when the implant is revealed in the Iron Ring scene. If a hero specifically asks about the flicker, a simple Insight check (Resist 3) confirms it didn't come from TC-663 or any external light source. That's all they get — the source is unknown.

DEMOS VARIANT: If Raden is delivered, Demos is visibly unsettled. He recognizes that these newcomers are pragmatic and dangerous — not the usual desperate chancers who wash up at court. He accelerates his own timeline, which affects later scenes.

TC-663 INTRODUCTION: During the audience, the silver protocol droid (TC-663 / 'Six-Six') translates for Varga. If the heroes use Switch's code phrase from Adventure 1, TC-663's photoreceptors flash recognition. He begins covertly assisting them — providing palace maps, guard rotations, and intelligence on Varga's operations. Without the code phrase, TC-663 remains cautious and provides only partial assistance. NOTE: If the heroes delivered Raden (dark path), TC-663 is visibly disturbed but still responds to Switch's code phrase. However, his trust in the heroes is diminished — he provides intel but watches them warily.

NARRATIVE FUNCTION: This scene establishes the heroes inside the fortress and introduces the key NPCs they'll interact with during the court phase. The tone varies dramatically based on their entry path — Path A feels like infiltrators walking a tightrope; Path B feels like predators who've already made their first kill.

encounters.name: Beat 1 — Skiff Across the Mist
encounters.trigger: Crew leaves Blackwind Point bound for the fortress dock
encounters.description:
The skiff glides out across Nymeve Lake through low banks of mist that wet the deck and cling to coats. The fortress materializes a piece at a time — a moss-eaten Republic-era ruin retrofitted with blaster turrets, gaudy banners bearing Varga's sigil, and a torch-lit landing platform ringed by a half-dozen Gamorrean dock guards. The skiff captain — a sullen Quarren — does not speak the entire crossing. He has done this run a thousand times and watched a fair number of his passengers come back in pieces.

This is the last quiet moment before the heroes are inside Varga's house. Use it. Whatever cover identities Raden and Varth coached them on in s3 Beat 4, this is when each PC walks themselves through the three-sentence pitch one more time. Path B (Raden delivered) crews spend the crossing watching their gift sit in the bow with a bag over his head and his hands behind his back. Nobody talks. The Quarren glances at the bag once and then forces himself to stop looking.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE BEAT — atmosphere and re-anchoring. The GM should describe the fortress assembling out of the mist in three passes: first the silhouette, then the turrets, then the guards. Use this beat to surface any cover-identity work the players want to revisit before they walk through the door. If the crew has the [Switch's code phrase] from Adventure 1, this is the right moment to remind them — TC-663 is going to be on the dais and they only get one chance to use it cleanly. WEAPON CONFISCATION: Gamorreans at the dock will pat the crew down at Beat 2's threshold. Anyone planning to keep a hold-out blaster declares it now — the Skulduggery / Conceal check happens in Beat 2 and is gated on having flagged the intent here. Path B variant: when the bag-and-bound prisoner is offloaded, one of the dock Gamorreans looks at the bag, looks at the crew, and grunts a Huttese laugh. He recognizes the silhouette already.

encounters.name: Beat 2 — Through the Dock and Into the Throne Room
encounters.trigger: Crew is escorted off the skiff and through the lower corridors
encounters.description:
Damp, torch-lit corridors smelling of mold and roasting meat. Gamorrean tusks scrape stone overhead. A Twi'lek attendant in worn-out finery confiscates weapons at the threshold — anyone trying to keep something hidden rolls now. Then the doors open and the heroes are spilled into Varga's Throne Room: a sensory assault of thick spice smoke, frantic jizz-wailer music, and a crowd of sycophants, thieves, and scavengers parting to either side of a long carpeted approach.

At the far end, on a massive electrum-plated hover-sled, sits Varga the Hutt — bloated, scarred, flanked on his right by the silver protocol droid TC-663 and on his left by Igren Demos, the Neimoidian majordomo. Varga barks in Huttese without looking up from the platter in front of him. TC-663 translates with exaggerated courtesy.

**PATH FORK lands here.** Path A: 'The Mighty Varga is bored with beggars. Prove you are worth his air.' (continues to Beat 3 — auditions). Path B: 'You bring me a GIFT — the thief who stole from Besadii, delivered to my feet like a wrapped present!' (skips Beat 3 entirely, goes straight to Beat 4 — Raden recognized).

As Varga shifts his weight to look at the crew properly, the heroes catch it — a faint blue flicker near his right temple, gone before anyone can focus on it. Probably a reflection off TC-663's chassis. Probably.
encounters.tactics:
PATH FORK BEAT. The GM resolves the path here based on the s3 / s4 decision-point flag (`raden-fate`):
  • `light` or `threaten` → Path A → continue to Beat 3.
  • `dark` → Path B → skip Beat 3 entirely and resolve Beat 4's dark-path branch immediately.

WEAPON CONCEALMENT (optional, only if flagged in Beat 1): Skulduggery vs Resist 4. Mastery means a hold-out blaster makes it past the pat-down. Failure means the Twi'lek attendant pulls the weapon out, holds it up theatrically, and Varga laughs — no immediate consequence other than a -1 to that PC's audition resist (Varga is amused, not insulted), but the crew has now established that they tried to smuggle a weapon and Demos files it.

CYBERNETIC BREADCRUMB #1: The blue flicker at Varga's right temple. Do NOT explain. If a player passes Insight at Resist 4, they confirm it wasn't a reflection — something is implanted in his skull. This breadcrumb pays off in p2-s2 (Iron Ring) and p2-s3 (implant identification). If Beat 5's TC-663 conversation runs and the courier-implant topic surfaces, this is the breadcrumb that connects.

TC-663 RECOGNITION: If the crew has the Switch code phrase from Adv1 and uses it now — directly to TC-663 in front of Varga — it is a disaster. The phrase is meant for a private moment. Demos will hear it, file it, and the entire infiltration is on a clock. Steer players toward saving the phrase for Beat 5. If they insist, Demos's Insight against the speaker is at Resist 4 — failure means the phrase is overheard and Demos starts watching that PC for the rest of the court phase (+1 resist on all that PC's social checks until end of part 1).

encounters.name: Beat 3 — The Auditions (Path A only)
encounters.trigger: Path A — Varga demands a demonstration of worth from each PC
encounters.description:
Varga waves the heroes forward one at a time. He has a different test for each archetype and the court watches closely — courtiers placing side-bets in Huttese while TC-663 translates the patter dryly.

**The Muscle** is sent into the side pit against a Gamorrean (smaller cousin of Gorrak — non-lethal exhibition). **The Face** is set against a circle of Varga's courtiers in a battle of wits — a fast-cutting verbal joust where the courtiers try to make the PC look provincial. **The Tech** is handed a multi-tool and ordered to fix Varga's hover-sled with a Gamorrean's blaster pressed gently behind the ear. **All other PCs** make a Deception check to maintain the cover identity they workshopped in s3 Beat 4 — Varga's eyes linger on anyone who isn't actively performing.

The four discipline checks for this scene (`sc-a2s2-melee`, `sc-a2s2-charm`, `sc-a2s2-tech`, `sc-a2s2-deception`) all live in this beat. Resolve them in the order Varga calls each PC up — typically loudest specialty first, deception last as the residual scrutiny check.
encounters.tactics:
PRIMARY MECHANICAL BEAT (Path A only). Run the existing four discipline challenges here.

COVER-STORY WORKSHOP WIRING: Apply the per-PC resist modifiers from s3 Beat 4 to the Deception check (`sc-a2s2-deception` — see its `resistModifiers` field). The base resist is 4; modify per PC based on the quality of their workshopped pitch:
  • Strong, in-voice pitch (hook/brag/price matched the sheet): -1 resist.
  • Adequate pitch: standard resist (4).
  • Vague or off-tone pitch: +1 resist.
  • Workshop didn't happen because Raden bolted (Comfort 1) or refused to coach (Comfort 2): ALL pitches at +1 resist.

COVER WEAPON FUMBLE (from Beat 2): If a PC was caught smuggling a weapon during the pat-down, that PC's audition resist is reduced by 1 (Varga is entertained by the audacity).

COURT TONE: Varga wants spectacle, not competence. Reward narrative flair. The GM should prompt players to describe HOW they pass the test, not just IF — the court reaction (cheers, bored silence, scattered laughter) shapes Beat 5 access. Adequate performances earn 'guest' status. Spectacular performances earn run-of-the-court invitations from specific courtiers (which become hooks for p2 court scenes).

FAILURE CONSEQUENCES: A failed audition does NOT end the scene. Varga is amused either way — the crew is entertainment regardless. But each failed audition adds +1 resist to Igren Demos's Insight watch on that PC for the duration of the court phase, AND (per `sc-a2s2-deception` failure text) a deception failure puts Demos on direct observation duty (+1 resist on all subsequent court-phase checks for that PC). Stack these effects.

encounters.name: Beat 4 — Raden Recognized / Dark-Path Fork
encounters.trigger: Path A: between auditions, a courtier makes a passing reference to 'the Devaronian thief'. Path B: Varga calls for the gift to be unwrapped.
encounters.description:
**PATH A variant — Whispered Recognition.** Mid-audition, a courtier near the back of the room — one of the Iron Ring delegates Raden warned about — leans to a neighbor and asks, in carrying Huttese, whether anyone has heard from 'that Devaronian, the one who skimmed Besadii — Raden? Raden, was it?' The conversation drifts. TC-663's silver head turns a fraction, then turns back. Varga's eyes flick — for a single heartbeat — to the dungeon corridor, then back to the floor show. The crew now knows that Raden's name is alive in this room. If they kept Raden alive, they have to keep him alive, and they have to keep the connection between Raden and themselves invisible. Nobody is allowed to mention how the crew came to be standing here.

**PATH B variant — The Gift Unwrapped.** Varga gestures at the bag. Two Gamorreans yank it off Raden's head. The Devaronian blinks in the smoke and torchlight. The court goes quiet. Raden looks once at the heroes — recognition, betrayal, a kind of tired understanding. Then his eyes drop. Varga laughs, deep and rolling. 'Take the thief to the cells beneath the pit. I will decide his fate when I am entertained enough to think about it.' (via TC-663). Gamorreans drag Raden away. He does not struggle. He does not look back. The entire audition is skipped. The crew is welcomed with magnanimous warmth — they understand business. The execution clock has now started. (Triggers Part 2, Event 1 — Execution of Raden.)
encounters.tactics:
MORAL-WEIGHT BEAT. This is the scene's emotional climax regardless of which path the crew chose. Run it slow. Let the silence breathe.

PATH A handling: The Iron Ring courtier's mention is roleplay only — no dice. The GM should narrate Varga's micro-glance at the dungeon corridor. If a PC succeeds an Insight check (Resist 3) on Varga, they read 'unfinished business — he expected to have the Devaronian by now.' This primes Beat 5 conversations: TC-663 (if turned) will confirm Varga has been waiting on a Trandoshan delivery that never came. Players who hear that have explicit foreshadowing that hiding Raden is going to get harder, not easier.

PATH B handling: NO DICE — narrative beat. Set the destiny tag flag and move on. If any PC plays a destiny that interacts with corruption / dark side moments, this is when the GM should call out the destiny pip swap. Raden's quiet acceptance is the hard bit — the GM should resist any urge to let him beg. He told the crew in s3 conversation Beat 2 that he expected this. He meant it.

INTERVENTION ATTEMPT (Path B only): If a player tries to stop the Gamorreans, this is the existing decision-point — extremely dangerous, blows cover instantly. Per the scene's `decisions` block, violence in the throne room equals instant death. The GM should give one warning beat (TC-663 hisses 'Do NOT' under his breath as the Gamorreans pass) and then resolve the consequences as written if the player commits.

END-OF-BEAT FLAGS: Set `raden-status-court-phase` based on path:
  • Path A: 'hidden-asset' — Raden is alive and useful but his name is now in play.
  • Path B: 'condemned' — Raden is in the cells, execution clock running, p2-event-1 triggered.

encounters.name: Beat 5 — Settling Into Court (TC-663 Aside)
encounters.trigger: After the auditions resolve and Varga waves the heroes off to guest quarters
encounters.description:
Servants — most of them indentured, all of them watching from under their lashes — escort the crew through a stone corridor toward the guest wing. The throne room music fades. Torch sconces give way to badly-rewired glow strips bolted into the ceiling.

Halfway down the corridor, the silver protocol droid catches up. TC-663 walks at a precisely respectful three paces behind the lead servant, and at the next junction he murmurs — politely, in Basic, just loud enough — 'If the honored guests would care to inspect the household's wine inventory, I am authorized to provide a brief survey.' It is a nonsense errand. It is also a way to peel one or two heroes off the escort group for a private moment in a service alcove off the corridor.

WHETHER TC-663 OPENS UP DEPENDS ON THE SWITCH CODE PHRASE. If the crew uses the Switch code phrase from Adventure 1 — privately, here in the alcove, NOT in the throne room — TC-663 visibly relaxes a millimeter and says: 'Master Switch sends his regards.' The conversation overlay opens. If the crew has no code phrase, or wastes the chance by using it in front of Demos in Beat 2, TC-663's aside is a flat-voiced inventory of the wine cellar with one half-veiled hint about the eastern corridor patrol pattern, and the crew settles into their rooms without an inside asset.
encounters.tactics:
GM ACTION (if Switch code phrase is used cleanly): Open the Conversation panel in the Command Bridge and launch [tc663-turned]. Players ask questions through the player overlay; GM delivers TC-663's responses one beat at a time. TC-663 starts at Comfort 3 — better than Raden (Comfort 2), worse than Maya (Comfort 4), reflecting that the droid has chosen this conversation but is genuinely worried about a Gamorrean shift change cutting it short.

The droid's exit lever is a footstep in the corridor — Demos doing a casual sweep, or a Gamorrean rounding the corner with a tray. The GM should drop one of these in the moment the conversation feels done OR the moment comfort drops to 1.

NO CODE PHRASE FALLBACK: If the crew has nothing to offer, TC-663 says quietly: 'The eastern corridor is less frequently patrolled after the third watch.' That single sentence — flavor only — and then he excuses himself. The crew goes to their rooms with a working palace but no inside asset. They can still recruit TC-663 in p2 if they identify themselves to him through other channels (e.g., showing him slicing credentials he recognizes), but it costs an in-fiction day and blows the timing on at least one p2 scene.

DARK-PATH VARIANT (Path B only): If the crew delivered Raden, TC-663 still meets them in the alcove if they have the code phrase, but the conversation opens with him grimmer than usual. The droid's first volunteered line — before the players ask anything — is: 'I observed the Devaronian's escort to the cells. Master Switch will be informed of the choice you made.' This does NOT change Switch's willingness to help (he is a slicer, not a moralist), but TC-663's `darkPathOpener` line in the conversation file colors the rest of the conversation. Players running the dark path will feel the room change.

END OF SCENE: Once the conversation closes (whether or not it ran), the crew is shown to guest quarters. Doors lock from the outside. The court phase has begun. Hand off to Part 2.

control.failure: Flat performance. Varga yawns. Cover survives but barely — you're furniture, not a guest.

scenes.title: The Gladiator Arena
scenes.subtitle: Day One — Blood Sport
scenes.readAloud:
The fortress shakes with the roar of a thousand voices. Varga's gladiator arena is carved into the rock beneath the main hall — a natural cavern expanded with durasteel walls and repulsor barriers. Torchlight and glow-rods throw shifting shadows across the sand floor.

Varga the Hutt watches from a hovering observation platform, attended by servants and sycophants. His enormous eyes glitter with anticipation.

As the fighters below warm up, Varga rumbles to a courtier beside him — rattling off credit figures with impossible precision. 'Forty-seven thousand, two hundred and fourteen credits on the Trandoshan. Twelve thousand, nine hundred and eighty-one against. The margin is unacceptable.' No datapad. No ledger. The numbers pour from memory like he's reading a display you can't see.

"Our new arrivals," he announces in Huttese, his booming voice filling the cavern. "Let us see what they are worth."

The arena gate opposite you grinds open. Out steps a massive Trandoshan — scarred, muscled, and grinning with far too many teeth. His name, chanted by the crowd, is Gorrak.

He cracks his knuckles. The crowd screams louder.
scenes.gmNotes:
This is the heroes' first test in Varga's court — a gladiatorial exhibition match. Varga uses these fights to evaluate newcomers and entertain his guests. Winning earns respect and access; losing earns contempt (but not death — Varga doesn't waste useful assets).

GORRAK is Varga's champion — a Trandoshan pit fighter who has survived 47 arena bouts. He fights with controlled brutality. He's dangerous but not trying to kill — this is sport, not war. If the heroes win, Gorrak nods respect and becomes a neutral contact in the fortress. If they lose, he offers a hand up. Either way, Varga is watching.

TACTICAL MAP ZONES: The pit has 16 distinct zones. Key tactical features: the Fallen Columns (west) are the only hard cover. The Trophy Stakes (east of center) and Chain Mounts (west wall) offer improvised weapons. The Bone Pit (southwest) is hazardous difficult terrain. The Sand Hollow (southeast) slows movement but offers concealment. The Cargo Lift (southeast corner) is Varga's surprise tool — he can raise a second opponent or a beast mid-fight. The Judgment Stone (south-center) is where defeated fighters kneel — dragging Gorrak there is a crowd-pleasing finish. The Control Station (south wall) lets a Tech-skilled hero manipulate the environment. Gorrak knows this terrain intimately — the heroes do not.

CYBERNETIC BREADCRUMB #2: Before the fight begins, Varga rattles off exact credit figures for the wagering pool — precise to the individual credit — without consulting any external device or ledger. This is the courier cybernetic's financial recall function at work. Varga accesses the implant's data unconsciously at this point, the way someone checks a mental note. An Insight or Investigation check (Resist 3) reveals that this level of recall is abnormal — Hutts have excellent memories but not eidetic financial precision across multiple accounts. Something is augmenting him. This is the second planted breadcrumb; combined with the flicker from the throne room, attentive players should start forming questions.

CROWD DYNAMICS: The crowd's reaction matters. A spectacular fight (high-tier results on combat checks) earns Varga's personal attention. A boring fight earns indifference. The court is watching to decide if these newcomers are worth cultivating. Using the environment creatively — grabbing trophy weapons, fighting around the columns, forcing an opponent onto the Judgment Stone — earns crowd approval.

SCENE PURPOSE: Establish the heroes' reputation in Varga's court. The gladiator fight is a set-piece combat encounter — the main event — surrounded by simple social checks for reading the crowd and impressing the right people. This scene sets up everything that follows: better performance here means easier access to NPCs, intel, and opportunities in later scenes.

- Arena fight vs Gorrak: SET-PIECE (full combat encounter, environment mechanics, crowd factor)
- Reading the crowd: SIMPLE (single Insight check, flavor + minor advantage)
- Impressing Varga: SIMPLE (single Charm/Deception check, reputation modifier)

scenes.title: The Iron Ring
scenes.subtitle: Day Two — Slavers and Poison
scenes.readAloud:
The fortress mood shifts on the second day. A delegation arrives from the Iron Ring — a slave-trading syndicate that operates across the Outer Rim. Their leader is a tattooed Zabrak named Vel Crekk, flanked by Trandoshan enforcers and a shuffling line of chained captives.

Varga receives them in the great hall, the air thick with incense and tension. The Iron Ring wants exclusive slaving rights in Varga's territory. Varga wants a percentage he hasn't earned.

Then it happens. Mid-negotiation, Vel Crekk disputes a supply figure. Varga makes an annoyed sound — and presses two thick fingers behind his right ear. A holographic ledger blooms from the side of his skull. Blue light, sharp lines, scrolling columns of numbers projected from inside his head. He scrolls through it with a flick of his fingers, stabs at a figure, and barks a correction at Vel Crekk. Then he releases the pressure and the hologram winks out. No one in the court reacts. They've seen this before.

You have not.

Among the delegation, you notice two figures of interest. A towering Wookiee named Grakkus — Iron Ring muscle, standing with arms folded and rage barely contained behind flat black eyes. And a thin, quiet human named Narek who moves with the servants, carrying a tray of drinks. He makes eye contact with you once. Just once.

Something is wrong with those drinks.
scenes.gmNotes:
The Iron Ring delegation is a political event with a hidden subplot: assassination by poison.

THE SURFACE: Vel Crekk and the Iron Ring are negotiating slaving rights with Varga. The heroes are expected to attend as part of Varga's court. The negotiation itself is background texture — the heroes aren't involved in the deal. But they're watching, and they can learn.

THE POISON: Narek is a former slave who has infiltrated the delegation. He has laced Varga's drinks with a slow-acting neurotoxin. His plan: kill the Hutt and free the captives in the chaos. It's desperate, it's doomed (Hutts are resistant to most poisons), and it puts the heroes in a moral bind.

IF DETECTED: The heroes spot the poison via Insight. They must choose:
- Warn Varga → earns enormous trust but condemns Narek to death
- Warn Narek → saves him but the assassination attempt may still trigger, blowing the heroes' cover
- Do nothing → the poison fails (Hutt biology), Varga gets sick but survives, and the investigation afterward threatens everyone's cover
- Swap the drinks → requires Skulduggery, prevents the attempt entirely, Narek is confused but alive

CYBERNETIC BREADCRUMB #3 — THE KEY REVEAL: During the negotiation with Vel Crekk, Varga activates his courier cybernetic openly for the first time. He presses two fingers behind his right ear and a holographic ledger projects from the side of his skull — blue light, scrolling financial columns, projected from an embedded device. This is a Cybot Galactica Model VII courier cybernetic, surgically implanted behind his right ear with a maintenance diagnostic port accessible externally. The court doesn't react because they've seen it before. The heroes should be stunned.

This is the 'oh no' moment. The account location data isn't stored externally — it's inside Varga's head. The crew cannot steal a device. They need to understand what this implant is, what it contains, and how to access the data. This fundamentally changes the mission from 'steal a thing' to 'investigate a person.'

IF HEROES HAVE A RECORDING ROD: They can capture the holographic projection. This preserved evidence becomes critical intelligence for TC-663 and Gome conversations in Working the Court. Without a recording, they must describe what they saw from memory.

DISCIPLINE CHECK: An Investigation or Tech check (Resist 3) can identify the device type. Masterful+ identifies it as a courier-class cybernetic — designed for secure data transport, military-grade encryption, built to survive the carrier's death. The data doesn't just live in Varga's head — it IS the secure vault.

GRAKKUS: The Wookiee enforcer is watching everything. He's not Iron Ring leadership — he's muscle. But he's smart muscle. He notices things. He'll reappear in Scene 6 (Knife in the Dark) as one of the assassins sent after the heroes.

MORAL WEIGHT: Narek is sympathetic — he's a freed slave trying to kill a slaver. But his plan endangers the heroes' mission. This is the first moral gray area the heroes face in Varga's court.

CHALLENGE COMPLEXITY:
- Poison detection: COMPLEX (Insight check with escalating consequences based on timing)
- Reading Vel Crekk: SIMPLE (single Insight check, intel gathering)
- Intervening with Narek: COMPLEX (multi-step social challenge depending on chosen approach)
- Swapping drinks: SIMPLE (single Skulduggery check if chosen)
- Reading Grakkus: SIMPLE (single Insight check, threat assessment)

scenes.title: Working the Court
scenes.subtitle: Between Events — The Long Game
scenes.readAloud:
Between the spectacles and delegations, the fortress settles into its rhythms. Servants carry trays through torchlit corridors. Guards change shifts at predictable intervals. Courtiers gossip in alcoves, trade favors over sabacc tables, and jockey for Varga's attention.

This is the quiet work — the real work. While the court is distracted, you can move. Explore the fortress. Build relationships. Gather the intelligence you need.

The protocol droid TC-663 passes you in the corridor. His photoreceptors linger a moment longer than necessary. He knows why you're here.

In the accounting wing, the Muun named Gome pores over financial ledgers, muttering about exchange rates. He likes to talk. About everything.

You saw what came out of Varga's skull during the Iron Ring negotiation. A holographic ledger, projected from inside his head. Whatever data Varth needs — the account locations, the financial pipeline — it's locked inside a cybernetic implant embedded in a Hutt's skull. You can't steal it. You can't slice it remotely. You need to understand what it is, what it contains, and whether there's any way to access it. TC-663 and Gome are your best leads.
scenes.gmNotes:
This is the investigation and relationship-building scene — the connective tissue between the set-piece court events. The heroes have downtime between Days 1-4 to explore, cultivate contacts, and investigate the courier cybernetic they witnessed in the Iron Ring scene.

STRUCTURE: This scene is a sandbox with structured simple checks. The GM runs it as freeform exploration punctuated by the specific challenges listed below. It can be interleaved with Scenes 1, 2, and 4 — exploration happens in the gaps between events.

KEY OBJECTIVES:
1. ACTIVATE TC-663: If the heroes have Switch's code phrase from Adventure 1, this is trivially easy (T0/P0). If not, it's a complex Charm challenge. TC-663 provides palace maps, guard rotations, AND — critically — identifies the implant as a Cybot Galactica Model VII courier cybernetic with a maintenance diagnostic port behind the right ear. He knows the model because he maintains Varga's medical records.
2. CULTIVATE GOME: The Muun accountant loves to talk about money. Charming him reveals Varga's Bespin escape route, Cloud City banking connections, and the name 'Figg & Associates.' Critical for Adventure 3. KEY INSIGHT: Gome also confirms that Varga's external accounts don't contain the data the heroes are looking for — 'Those accounts aren't on my systems. Whatever the boss keeps in that thing in his head, it's not mirrored anywhere I can see.' This confirms the implant is the sole repository.
3. FORTRESS RECONNAISSANCE: Stealth checks to map guard patrols, identify restricted areas, and scout the fortress layout for the eventual escape.
4. COVER MAINTENANCE: Ongoing Deception checks to maintain cover identity under increasing scrutiny.

CONDITIONAL: KESSRA'S AVIARY AMBUSH — If the heroes investigated the Vipers' camp too aggressively in Part 1 Scene 1, Kessra (the Vipers' Zygerrian leader) may have followed them to the fortress. She has released her trained Takodana Raptors in the aviary garden as an ambush. This is a conditional combat encounter that only triggers if the GM determines Kessra has cause for revenge.

CHALLENGE COMPLEXITY:
- TC-663 activation (with code phrase): SIMPLE (auto-success or trivial check)
- TC-663 activation (without code phrase): COMPLEX (multi-step Charm with trust-building)
- Gome cultivation: COMPLEX (extended social challenge with escalating intel)
- Fortress recon: SIMPLE (single Stealth check per area)
- Cover maintenance: SIMPLE (single Deception check per day)
- Kessra ambush: SET-PIECE (full combat encounter, conditional)

scenes.title: The Imperial Shadow
scenes.subtitle: Day Three — Lady Sinde
scenes.readAloud:
A shuttle descends through the canopy — Imperial design, unmarked. The ramp lowers and a woman steps out, flanked by four Stormtroopers in standard white armor. She wears a crisp Imperial uniform, rank insignia identifying her as a logistics officer.

Varga receives her in the throne room with unusual formality. She introduces herself as Lady Sinde, representing the Imperial Logistics Corps, here to discuss 'supply chain efficiencies' with Varga's operation.

Everything about her is wrong. Her boots are military issue — not logistics corps. Her eyes scan the room like a threat assessment, not a supply audit. The Stormtroopers with her don't behave like an honor guard. They behave like operators.

She glances at you once. Catalogues you. Moves on.

Later that evening, you notice her slipping away from the feast toward Varga's private wing. Alone.
scenes.gmNotes:
Lady Sinde is ISB — Imperial Security Bureau, embedded in the logistics corps as cover. She is here investigating Project Leviathan's supply chain, specifically the Tibanna gas pipeline between Varga and an Imperial source. She is NOT here for the heroes.

SINDE'S AGENDA: She suspects Imperial corruption — someone in the military hierarchy is siphoning resources through Varga's network. She doesn't know who (it's Varth). She is dangerous, competent, and not an enemy unless the heroes make her one. In fact, her investigation parallels theirs. She's a potential ally — or a catastrophic threat to their cover.

THE PRIVATE MEETING: Sinde meets with Varga privately to apply pressure. The heroes can eavesdrop (Stealth check) to learn critical intel: shipment coordinates, payment terms, mentions of 'the Accountant' (Varth's codename in Varga's records), and Sinde's veiled threats about Imperial audits.

SCENE PURPOSE: This scene introduces the Imperial dimension of the conspiracy. Until now, the heroes have been operating in the criminal underworld. Sinde represents the Empire's own interest in the same pipeline — and her presence means the heroes' window is closing. If the ISB finds what the heroes are looking for first, the evidence disappears into Imperial classified files forever.

CYBERNETIC URGENCY THREAD: Sinde's arrival accelerates Varga's paranoia. During the eavesdropped meeting, Varga mentions preparing to 'move operations to the contingency location' — Bespin. He's not just nervous about the audit; he's preparing to flee. The heroes realize their window to investigate the implant further is closing. Once Varga leaves Takodana, the cybernetic data goes with him. This urgency feeds into The Best Laid Plans (Scene 5) where the crew finalizes their extraction plan under time pressure.

CHALLENGE COMPLEXITY:
- Investigating Sinde's identity: COMPLEX (multi-step investigation with escalating revelations)
- Eavesdropping on the private meeting: COMPLEX (Stealth with significant consequences for failure)
- Avoiding Stormtrooper detection: SIMPLE (single check when entering restricted areas)
- Reading Sinde's body language at the feast: SIMPLE (single Insight check, threat assessment)

scenes.title: The Best Laid Plans
scenes.subtitle: Night Four — The Extraction Plan
scenes.readAloud:
Night four. The fortress corridors are quiet — the late feast winding down, servants clearing plates, guards settling into the graveyard shift.

Your crew gathers in your quarters. The door is locked. The Recording Rod plays back the Iron Ring hologram — Varga's skull projecting a ledger of accounts, routing numbers, financial infrastructure. A courier cybernetic embedded in a Hutt's skull.

TC-663's intel is spread across the table: implant model, diagnostic port location, guard rotations, escape routes. Gome's ramblings have been distilled into three words: Figg & Associates, Bespin.

The picture is clear. The data is inside Varga's head — literally. It can't be sliced remotely. It can't be copied without physical access to the diagnostic port. And Varga is preparing to flee to Cloud City.

You're laying out the approach — access routes, timing windows, contingencies — when Varth's voice cuts through the comlink:

"Movement in the corridor outside your quarters. Three contacts. Armed. This isn't a patrol."

The lock clicks. Not forced — opened with a code.

You're out of time.
scenes.gmNotes:
This scene replaces the former datapad heist. There is NO standalone heist — the crew never gets a clean shot at Varga's implant. Instead, this scene serves two purposes:

1. PLANNING CONSOLIDATION: The crew reviews everything they've gathered — the Iron Ring hologram recording, TC-663's implant identification (Cybot Galactica Model VII, diagnostic port behind right ear), Gome's Bespin/Cloud City/Figg & Associates intel, and the urgency created by Sinde's ISB audit accelerating Varga's departure. This is the moment the crew synthesizes their investigation into a plan.

2. INTERRUPTED BY KNIFE IN THE DARK: The planning session is cut short by the assassination attempt (Scene 6). The crew never gets to execute their extraction plan because violence erupts first. This is deliberate — the narrative intention is that the crew escapes Takodana with intelligence ABOUT the cybernetic, not data FROM it. The actual data extraction happens on Bespin in Adventure 3.

NO STANDALONE ENCOUNTERS OR DISCIPLINE CHECKS: This scene has no mechanical challenges of its own. It is a narrative bridge — the crew reviews their intel, begins formulating a plan, and is interrupted by the Scene 6 assassination attempt. The GM should use this scene to:
- Confirm what the crew knows (implant model, diagnostic port, Bespin escape route)
- Let them debate approaches (physical access vs. convincing Varga vs. intercepting on Bespin)
- Establish the time pressure (Varga is leaving SOON)
- Then slam the door open with assassins

VARTH'S ROLE: Varth provides tactical awareness via comlink — he warns the crew about the assassins approaching. This reinforces his competence and makes his later betrayal more painful. He's genuinely useful here.

WHAT THE CREW ESCAPES WITH: NOT the account data. They escape with:
- TC-663's implant specs (Model VII, diagnostic port location)
- Gome's Bespin intel (Cloud City, Figg & Associates)
- The Recording Rod capture of the Iron Ring hologram
- Varga's escape trajectory (from Scene 9)
- The knowledge that the data is ONLY in Varga's head

TRANSITION: This scene flows directly into Scene 6 (Knife in the Dark). The assassination erupts before the extraction plan can be executed. From there, the cascade is: assassination → dungeon → escape → hangar.

scenes.title: Knife in the Dark
scenes.subtitle: Night — Assassination Attempt
scenes.readAloud:
You wake to the sound of something wrong.

Not a noise — the absence of noise. The fortress hum is still there, the distant rumble of generators and the drip of jungle condensation. But the corridor outside your quarters has gone silent. No guard footsteps. No droid patrol.

Then: a shadow moves at the edge of your door. Too low for a guard. Too fast for a servant.

The lock clicks. Not forced — opened with a code.

Three figures slide into the room. The first is massive — a Wookiee, moving with terrifying silence for something that size. Grakkus. Behind him, lean and quiet, is Skreev — the Rodian bounty hunter from the Vipers. And behind both of them, face hidden in shadow, is Narek.

They're here to kill you.
scenes.gmNotes:
This is a nighttime assassination attempt — a combat ambush in the heroes' quarters. The attackers are a coalition of threats the heroes have accumulated during their time in the court.

ATTACKER COMPOSITION:
- GRAKKUS (Wookiee enforcer): He flagged the heroes as threats during the Iron Ring delegation. Overwhelming close combat specialist — Wookiee strength in confined quarters. The muscle.
- SKREEV (Rodian bounty hunter): From the Vipers in Part 1. Has been tracking the heroes since they entered the fortress. The professional.
- NAREK (conditional): Only present if the heroes exposed or humiliated him during the poison subplot. If the heroes helped him or he escaped cleanly, Narek is NOT among the assassins. Replace with an additional Iron Ring enforcer.

AMBUSH CONDITIONS: The heroes are in their quarters. Weapons may not be immediately accessible (Skulduggery check to have stashed weapons within reach). Armor is not worn. Lighting is minimal. The attackers have surprise unless the heroes succeed on an Awareness check.

SCENE PURPOSE: This is the consequence scene — the court's dangers catching up. The assassination interrupts the crew's extraction planning from Scene 5 (The Best Laid Plans). They were laying out an approach to Varga's courier cybernetic when the door opened. After this fight, the investigation phase is over — everything that follows is survival, rescue, and escape. The crew leaves Takodana with intelligence about the implant, not data from it.

IF THE HEROES CAPTURE AN ASSASSIN: Interrogation reveals that the hit was contracted by someone inside the court — not Varga himself. The contract came through Demos. This is Demos testing the heroes (if he's suspicious) or removing potential rivals (if the heroes are too successful).

CHALLENGE COMPLEXITY:
- Waking up in time: SIMPLE (single Awareness check, determines surprise)
- The fight itself: SET-PIECE (full combat encounter, environment mechanics, multiple enemies)
- Stashed weapons: SIMPLE (single Skulduggery check, retroactive preparation)
- Interrogation afterward: COMPLEX (if an assassin is captured alive)
